readings.title: Ḥushai's Warning
readings.subtitle: Dawiḏ Escapes Across the Yardĕn
readings.text: [2 Samuel 17:15] And Ḥushai said to Tsaḏoq and Eḇyathar the priests, “Thus and so Aḥithophel counselled <dn>את</dn> Aḇshalom and the elders of Yisra’ĕl, and thus and so I have counselled. [16] “Now therefore, send quickly and inform Dawiḏ, saying, ‘Do not spend this night in the plains of the wilderness, but by all means pass over, lest the sovereign and all the people with him be swallowed up.’ ” [17] Now Yehonathan and Aḥima‛ats were staying at Ěn Rogĕl, for they could not be seen entering the city. And a female servant was to go and inform them, and they go and inform Sovereign Dawiḏ. [18] And a lad saw <dn>את</dn> them, and informed Aḇshalom. But both of them went away quickly and came to a man’s house in Baḥurim, who had a well in his courtyard, and they went down into it. [19] And the woman took and spread <dn>את</dn> a covering over the well’s mouth, and spread ground grain on it, so the matter was not known. [20] And Aḇshalom’s servants came to the woman at the house and said, “Where are Aḥima‛ats and Yehonathan?” And the woman said to them, “They have passed over the stream of water.” And they sought and did not find them, and returned to Yerushalayim. [21] And it came to be, after they had left, that they came up out of the well and went and informed Sovereign Dawiḏ, and said to Dawiḏ, “Rise up and pass over <dn>את</dn> the water quickly. For thus has Aḥithophel counselled against you.” [22] And Dawiḏ and all the people who were with him rose up and passed over <dn>את</dn> the Yardĕn. By morning light not even one was left who had not passed over <dn>את</dn> the Yardĕn. [23] And Aḥithophel saw that his counsel was not followed, so he saddled <dn>את</dn> his donkey, and arose and went home to his house, to his city. And he gave charge to his house, and hanged himself, and died. And he was buried in his father’s tomb. [24] And Dawiḏ went to Maḥanayim. And Aḇshalom passed over <dn>את</dn> the Yardĕn, he and all the men of Yisra’ĕl with him. [25] And Aḇshalom made <dn>את</dn> Amasa commander of the army instead of Yo’aḇ. Now Amasa was the son of a man whose name was Yithra, an Yisra’ĕlite, who had gone in to Aḇigal the daughter of Naḥash, sister of Tseruyah, Yo’aḇ’s mother. [26] And Yisra’ĕl and Aḇshalom pitched their tents in the land of Gil‛aḏ. [27] And it came to be, when Dawiḏ had come to Maḥanayim, that Shoḇi son of Naḥash from Rabbah of the children of Ammon, and Maḵir son of Ammi’ĕl from Lo Deḇar, and Barzillai the Gil‛aḏite from Rogelim, [28] brought beds and basins, and earthen vessels and wheat, and barley and flour, and roasted grain and beans, and lentils and roasted seeds, [29] and honey and curds, and sheep and cheese of the herd, for Dawiḏ and the people who were with him to eat. For they said, “The people are hungry and weary and thirsty in the wilderness.”

readings.title: The Battle in the Forest
readings.subtitle: The Death of Aḇshalom
readings.text: [2 Samuel 18:1] And Dawiḏ mustered <dn>את</dn> the people who were with him, and set commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds over them. [2] And Dawiḏ sent out <dn>את</dn> a third of the people under the hand of Yo’aḇ, and a third under the hand of Aḇishai son of Tseruyah, Yo’aḇ’s brother, and a third under the hand of Ittai the Gittite. And the sovereign said to the people, “I also shall certainly go out with you.” [3] But the people said, “You do not go out! For if we flee away, they are not going to care about us. And if half of us die, they are not going to care about us. But you are worth ten thousand of us. And now, it is better that you be to us a help from the city.” [4] And the sovereign said to them, “Whatever seems best to you I do.” And the sovereign stood beside the gate, and all the people went out by hundreds and by thousands. [5] And the sovereign commanded <dn>את</dn> Yo’aḇ and <dn>את</dn> Aḇishai and <dn>את</dn> Ittai, saying, “Gently, for my sake, with the young man Aḇshalom.” And all the people heard when the sovereign gave <dn>את</dn> all the commanders orders concerning Aḇshalom. [6] So the people went out into the field against Yisra’ĕl. And the battle was in the forest of Ephrayim. [7] And the people of Yisra’ĕl were smitten there before the servants of Dawiḏ, and the slaughter there that day was great, twenty thousand. [8] And the battle there was scattered over the face of all the country, and the forest devoured more people that day than the sword devoured. [9] And Aḇshalom met the servants of Dawiḏ. And Aḇshalom was riding on a mule. And the mule went under the thick boughs of a great oak, and his head caught in the oak. So he was suspended between the heavens and the earth. And the mule which was under him passed on. [10] And a certain man saw <dn>את</dn> Aḇshalom and informed Yo’aḇ, and said, “See, I saw <dn>את</dn> Aḇshalom hanging in an oak.” [11] And Yo’aḇ said to the man who informed him, “And see, you saw him! And why did you not smite him there to the ground? And it would have been on me to give you ten pieces of silver and a belt.” [12] And the man said to Yo’aḇ, “Even if I were to weigh a thousand pieces of silver in my hands, I would not put out <dn>את</dn> my hand against the son of the sovereign, for in our hearing the sovereign commanded <dn>את</dn> you and <dn>את</dn> Aḇishai and <dn>את</dn> Ittai, saying, ‘Beware, whoever it is, of the young man Aḇshalom!’ [13] “Else I would have dealt falsely against my own life. For no matter is hidden from the sovereign, and you yourself would have set yourself against me.” [14] And Yo’aḇ said, “I am not going to wait like this before you.” And he took three spears in his hand and thrust them through the heart of Aḇshalom, while he was still alive in the midst of the oak. [15] And ten young men who bore Yo’aḇ’s armour surrounded <dn>את</dn> Aḇshalom, and smote him and killed him. [16] And Yo’aḇ blew the ram’s horn, and the people returned from pursuing Yisra’ĕl, for Yo’aḇ held back <dn>את</dn> the people. [17] And they took <dn>את</dn> Aḇshalom and threw him into a large pit in the forest, and laid a very large heap of stones over him. And all Yisra’ĕl fled, each to his tent. [18] And Aḇshalom in his lifetime had taken and set up for himself <dn>את</dn> a pillar, which is in the Sovereign’s Valley. For he said, “I have no son to keep my name in remembrance.” And he called the pillar after his own name. And to this day it is called Aḇshalom’s Monument.

readings.title: Two Runners, One Message
readings.subtitle: The Sovereign Mourns His Son
readings.text: [2 Samuel 18:19] And Aḥima‛ats son of Tsaḏoq said, “Please let me run and bring the sovereign the message, that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has rightly ruled for him, out of the hand of his enemies.” [20] And Yo’aḇ said to him, “You are not the man to take the message today, but you shall take the message another day. But today you do not take a message, because the sovereign’s son is dead.” [21] And Yo’aḇ said to the Kushi, “Go, declare to the sovereign what you have seen.” And the Kushi bowed himself to Yo’aḇ, and ran. [22] And Aḥima‛ats son of Tsaḏoq said again to Yo’aḇ, “But whatever happens, please let me also run after the Kushi.” And Yo’aḇ said, “Why do you want to run, my son, since you have no message ready?” [23] “But whatever happens, let me run.” And he said to him, “Run.” Then Aḥima‛ats ran by way of the plain, and outran <dn>את</dn> the Kushi. [24] And Dawiḏ was sitting between the two gates. And the watchman went up to the roof over the gate, to the wall, and lifted <dn>את</dn> his eyes and looked and saw a man, running alone. [25] And the watchman cried out and informed the sovereign. And the sovereign said, “If he is alone, there is a message in his mouth.” And he came closer and closer. [26] And the watchman saw another man running, and the watchman called to the gatekeeper and said, “See, another man, running alone!” And the sovereign said, “He also brings a message.” [27] And the watchman said, “I see the running of the first is like the running of Aḥima‛ats son of Tsaḏoq.” And the sovereign said, “He is a good man, and comes with a good message.” [28] And Aḥima‛ats called out and said to the sovereign, “Peace!” And he bowed down to the earth on his face before the sovereign, and said, “Blessed be <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, who has delivered up <dn>את</dn> the men who raised their hand against my master the sovereign!” [29] And the sovereign said, “Is it well with the young man Aḇshalom?” And Aḥima‛ats answered, “When Yo’aḇ sent <dn>את</dn> the sovereign’s servant, and <dn>את</dn> me your servant, I saw a great crowd, but I did not know what it was.” [30] And the sovereign said, “Turn aside, stand here.” And he turned aside and stood still. [31] And see, the Kushi came, and the Kushi said, “Let my master the sovereign receive a message, that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has rightly ruled for you today, out of the hand of all those who rose up against you.” [32] And the sovereign said to the Kushi, “Is it well with the young man Aḇshalom?” And the Kushi answered, “Let the enemies of my master the sovereign, and all who rise against you for evil, be as that young man!” [33] And the sovereign was deeply moved, and went up to the room over the gate, and wept. And as he went, he said thus, “O my son Aḇshalom, my son, my son Aḇshalom! If only I had died instead of you! O Aḇshalom, my son, my son!”

readings.title: Yo'aḇ Rebukes the Sovereign
readings.subtitle: Yisra'ĕl Seeks to Bring Dawiḏ Back
readings.text: [2 Samuel 19:1] And it was reported to Yo’aḇ, “See, the sovereign is weeping and mourning for Aḇshalom.” [2] So the deliverance that day was turned into mourning for all the people. For the people heard it said that day, “The sovereign is grieved for his son.” [3] And the people stole back into the city that day, as people steal away when ashamed of fleeing in battle. [4] But the sovereign covered <dn>את</dn> his face, and the sovereign cried out with a loud voice, “O my son Aḇshalom! O Aḇshalom, my son, my son!” [5] And Yo’aḇ came into the house to the sovereign, and said, “Today you have shamed <dn>את</dn> the faces of all your servants who today have saved <dn>את</dn> your life, and <dn>את</dn> the lives of your sons and daughters, and <dn>את</dn> the lives of your wives and <dn>את</dn> the lives of your concubines, [6] by loving <dn>את</dn> your enemies and hating <dn>את</dn> your friends. For you have declared today that commanders and servants are naught to you. For today I know that if Aḇshalom had lived and all of us had died today, then it would have been right in your eyes. [7] “And now, rise up, go out and speak to the heart of your servants. For I swear by <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, if you do not go out, not one will stay with you this night. And that would be worse for you than all the evil that has come upon you from your youth until now.” [8] And the sovereign rose up and sat in the gate. And they declared to all the people, saying, “See, the sovereign is sitting in the gate.” And all the people came before the sovereign. For Yisra’ĕl had fled, each to his tent. [9] And all the people were disputing throughout all the tribes of Yisra’ĕl, saying, “The sovereign delivered us from the hand of our enemies, and he rescued us from the hand of the Philistines, and now he has fled from the land because of Aḇshalom. [10] “But Aḇshalom, whom we anointed over us, has died in battle. And now, why are you silent about bringing the sovereign back?” [11] And Sovereign Dawiḏ sent to Tsaḏoq and Eḇyathar the priests, saying, “Speak to the elders of Yehuḏah, saying, ‘Why are you the last to bring <dn>את</dn> the sovereign back to his house, since the words of all Yisra’ĕl have come to the sovereign, to his house? [12] ‘You are my brothers, you are my bone and my flesh. Why then are you the last to bring back <dn>את</dn> the sovereign?’ [13] “And say to Amasa, ‘Are you not my bone and my flesh? <dn>Elohim</dn> do so to me, and more also, if you are not commander of the army before me continually in place of Yo’aḇ.’ ” [14] So he bowed <dn>את</dn> the heart of all the men of Yehuḏah, as one man, and they sent word to the sovereign, “Return, you and all your servants.”

readings.title: Shim‛i's Confession
readings.subtitle: The Sovereign Crosses the Yardĕn
readings.text: [2 Samuel 19:15] And the sovereign returned and came to the Yardĕn. And Yehuḏah came to Gilgal, to go to meet the sovereign, to bring <dn>את</dn> the sovereign over <dn>את</dn> the Yardĕn. [16] And Shim‛i son of Gĕra, a Binyaminite, who was from Baḥurim, hurried and came down with the men of Yehuḏah to meet Sovereign Dawiḏ, [17] and a thousand men of Binyamin with him, and Tsiḇa the servant of the house of Sha’ul, and his fifteen sons and his twenty servants with him. And they rushed to the Yardĕn before the sovereign, [18] and a ferryboat went across to carry over <dn>את</dn> the sovereign’s household, and to do what was good in his eyes. And Shim‛i son of Gĕra fell down before the sovereign when he had passed over <dn>את</dn> the Yardĕn. [19] And he said to the sovereign, “Let not my master hold me guilty, nor remember the crookedness of your servant on the day that my master the sovereign went out of Yerushalayim, that the sovereign should take it to heart. [20] “For your servant knows that I have sinned. Therefore see, I have come today, the first of all the house of Yosĕph to go down to meet my master the sovereign.” [21] And Aḇishai son of Tseruyah answered and said, “Should not Shim‛i be put to death for this, because he cursed <dn>את</dn> the anointed of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>?” [22] And Dawiḏ said, “What have I to do with you, you sons of Tseruyah, that you should be an adversary to me today? Should any man be put to death today in Yisra’ĕl? For do I not know that today I am sovereign over Yisra’ĕl?” [23] And the sovereign said to Shim‛i, “You shall not die.” And the sovereign swore to him.

readings.title: Mephiḇosheth's Defense
readings.subtitle: A Divided Inheritance
readings.text: [2 Samuel 19:24] And Mephiḇosheth son of Sha’ul came down to meet the sovereign. And he had not cared for his feet, nor trimmed his moustache, nor washed his garments, from the day the sovereign departed until the day he returned in peace. [25] And it came to be, when he came to Yerushalayim to meet the sovereign, that the sovereign said to him, “Why did you not go with me, Mephiḇosheth?” [26] And he answered, “My master, O sovereign, my servant deceived me. For your servant said, ‘Let me saddle a donkey for myself, and ride on it, and go to the sovereign,’ because your servant is lame. [27] “And he has slandered your servant to my master the sovereign, but my master the sovereign is like a messenger of <dn>Elohim</dn>. So do what is good in your eyes. [28] “For all my father’s house were but dead men before my master the sovereign. Yet you set your servant among those who eat at your own table. Therefore what right have I still to cry out anymore to the sovereign?” [29] And the sovereign said to him, “Why do you speak anymore of your matters? I have said, ‘You and Tsiḇa divide <dn>את</dn> the land.’ ” [30] And Mephiḇosheth said to the sovereign, “Let him even take <dn>את</dn> it all, since my master the sovereign has come back in peace to his own house.”

readings.title: A Shield for Me
readings.subtitle: A Psalm of Dawiḏ When He Fled
readings.text: [Psalm 3:1] A Psalm of Dawiḏ when he fled from Aḇshalom his son. <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, how my adversaries have increased! Many are rising up against me. [2] Many are saying of me, “There is no deliverance for him in <dn>Elohim</dn>.” Selah. [3] But <dn>You</dn>, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, are a shield for me, my esteem, and the <dn>One</dn> who lifts up my head. [4] I cried to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> with my voice, and <dn>He</dn> heard me from <dn>His</dn> set-apart mountain. Selah. [5] I lay down and slept; I awoke, for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> sustained me. [6] I am not afraid of ten thousands of people who have set themselves against me all around. [7] Arise, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>; save me, O my <dn>Elohim</dn>! Because <dn>You</dn> have smitten <dn>את</dn> all my enemies on the cheek; <dn>You</dn> have broken the teeth of the wrong. [8] Deliverance belongs to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. <dn>Your</dn> blessing is on <dn>Your</dn> people. Selah.

readings.title: Earnestly I Seek You
readings.subtitle: A Psalm in the Wilderness
readings.text: [Psalm 63:1] A Psalm of Dawiḏ when he was in the wilderness of Yehuḏah. O <dn>Elohim</dn>, <dn>You</dn> are my <dn>Ěl</dn>; I earnestly seek <dn>You</dn>; my being has thirsted for <dn>You</dn>; my flesh has longed for <dn>You</dn> in a dry and thirsty land without water. [2] Therefore I have looked to <dn>You</dn> in the set-apart place, to see <dn>Your</dn> power and <dn>Your</dn> esteem. [3] Because <dn>Your</dn> loving-commitment is better than life, my lips do praise <dn>You</dn>. [4] Therefore I bless <dn>You</dn> while I live; in <dn>Your</dn> Name I lift up my hands. [5] My being is satisfied as with marrow and fatness, and my mouth praises <dn>You</dn> with singing lips. [6] When I remember <dn>You</dn> on my bed, I meditate on <dn>You</dn> in the night watches. [7] For <dn>You</dn> have been my help, and in the shadow of <dn>Your</dn> wings I sing. [8] My being has clung to <dn>You</dn>; <dn>Your</dn> right hand upholds me. [9] But those who seek my life, to destroy it, shall go into the lower parts of the earth. [10] They are given over to the power of the sword; they are a portion for jackals. [11] But the sovereign rejoices in <dn>Elohim</dn>; everyone who swears by <dn>Him</dn> exalts, for the mouth of those speaking falsehood is stopped.
